issue_context.title: Unable to cast TTS to Google Cast despite proper `external_url` set
issue_context.body:
### The problem

I have following configuration:

* `https://ha.domain.example` is publicly reachable and set as HA `external_url`
* `https://ha.internal.domain.example` is provided through PiHole in local network and set as `internal_url`.
* `*.internal.domain.example` resolves to generic "not found" error over internet.

My Nest device is unable to play TTS messages (see log section).

It would be useful to force use of external URL in such case, or at least fallback to it. 

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

2023.2.3

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant Container

### Integration causing the issue

Google Cast

### Link to integration documentation on our website

_No response_

### Diagnostics information

_No response_

### Example YAML snippet

_No response_

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

```txt
Failed to cast media https://ha.internal.domain.example/api/tts_proxy/640ab2bae07bedc4c163f679a746f7ab7fb5d1fa_en_-_google_translate.mp3 from internal_url (https://ha.internal.domain.example).

Please make sure the URL is: Reachable from the cast device and either a publicly resolvable hostname or an IP address
```


### Additional information

_No response_

Hi. If it helps anyone, I got it to work for local/internal_url, without SSL, on Docker.
- Instead of using the Google Cast integration, I installed Google Translate text-to-speech
- Changed the Home Assistant URL in Settings->System->Network to http://my-local-ip:8123
- Forwarded ports 5353 and 8009 to my container (Portainer)
- I set the internal_url in configuration.yaml to my-local-ip:8123, but this is ignored, according to the container log
- I altered automations to use the Google Translate entity
- Enabled mDNS and IGMP snooping on the network (Unifi)

>I found a workaround which seems to work so far: I have the Mini on a dedicated smart home VLAN and I setup a block for Google's DNS IPs (8.8.8.8 and 8.8.4.4) on that VLAN. It appears that the Mini correctly falls back onto the DHCP-provided DNS server in that case and that allows it to resolve my local HA domain (provided by my Pi Hole). This likely will only work if your local address is a domain and is provided by your local DNS server.

@Friendly0Fire This is brilliant! It works flawlessly for me, thanks. I'm curious why would Google ignore conventions and prefer their DNS servers in the first place.

> 8.8.8.8 and 8.8.4.4

Wow! This works for me. Thanks for the hint.

For all Unifi users: I just blocked used the new Unifi Zone Firewall and configured that all "untrusted" devices cannot access both IP addresses in the "external" network.

The error message in the OP explains the problem quite well:
```
Failed to cast media https://ha.internal.domain.example/api/tts_proxy/640ab2bae07bedc4c163f679a746f7ab7fb5d1fa_en_-_google_translate.mp3 from internal_url (https://ha.internal.domain.example).

Please make sure the URL is: Reachable from the cast device and either a publicly resolvable hostname or an IP address
```

I'm not sure how to solve this issue in a way where it works for everyone.

Blocking the cast devices from using Google's public DNS servers doesn't seem like a good option.

Does it at least consistently work if setting the internal url to an IP-address?

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/22464818-0bf8-46c8-a3a1-7ef11fb4ed2e)

> I'm not sure how to solve this issue in a way where it works for everyone.

I think adding option `prefer: 'external' | 'internal'` with default to `internal` would be enough.

Thinking about it some more, I think the solution has to be to set the `internal_url` (local network in the UI) to a URL using an IP-address.
Or is there any case this is not good enough and will not work?

> Or is there any case this is not good enough

Yes, internal URL is used by multiple other services, and it's not always desirable to have it exposed (even for reasons it looks ugly), or even have hard-coded IP address. My home server has everything going through nginx, TLS with logged access.

OK, but it's a well known limitation of Google Chromecast devices and Android devices that they fall back to Google's DNS servers.

Hence, the `internal_url` needs to be either an IP-address, or a publicly resolvable hostname, or you need to do some tricks to keep the Google devices from calling home to Google, for example block the Google DNS servers, or redirect traffic to Google's DNS servers to your own DNS server.

The default, recommended and supported configuration is to set the `internal_url` to an IP-address.

Using the `external_url` is not correct, because the devices are on your internal network. Moreover, if you're a Home Assistant cloud user, traffic will be routed via the cloud meaning playing local media will not work when the internet connection is down, and the extra bandwidth usage is also an issue.

> OK, but it's a well known limitation of Google Chromecast devices and Android devices that they fall back to Google's DNS servers.

The problem isn't that they *fall back* to Google's DNS servers, it's the reverse: they fall back to the DHCP provided DNS server only if Google's DNS is inaccessible. That's a terrible design decision, but it's one we're stuck with.

I've been blocking Google's DNS for years now and it's been completely fine. No loss of functionality, no need to have `internal_url` point to an IP address (which I also couldn't do since my HA instance is on a Docker server with tons of other services listening to 443 with different hostnames).

> The problem isn't that they fall back to Google's DNS servers, it's the reverse

My understanding is there's some very aggressive validation of the DNS servers provided by DHCP, with a fallback to Google's DNS servers, but maybe it's like you state.

> I've been blocking Google's DNS for years now and it's been completely fine.

No one will stop you from doing that, but it's not a solution we can recommend.

Well then honestly there should just be a way to override the URL provided to Google devices specifically. I want to preserve my local domain for general use in HA, but if I could point those devices to an internal IP on a separate port, then there'd be no issues.

I understand it's hacky and complicated, but I think that's the only permanent solution.

> there should just be a way to override the URL provided to Google devices specifically
> ...
> that's the only permanent solution

It's still not clear to me why it's a problem to set the host of the `internal_url` to an IP address. The only use of the `internal_url` is for Home Assistant to calculate a URLs on which other devices can fetch some resource, it's not meant for humans.

If you want something which humans can memorize, you can have that too of course, it just won't be used when Home Assistant generates URLs for machine consumption.

You did mention you have some vhost setup, but I don't understand why that's a blocking issue; you could setup nginx to listen to an additional port or just expose an appropriate homeassistant docker port as well as the vhost forward.

I've looked around and I genuinely do not see anywhere saying that `internal_url` is not meant for humans. It's the default URL used by the app when on the local network. Filling in `external_url` is only explained in the "remote access" section of the user manual.

I personally won't be changing my configuration regardless since it works fine as is, but I'm pretty surprised by this response. You guys need to update a lot of documentation and forum discussions if that's the intended way to interpret those two config options.

> I've looked around and I genuinely do not see anywhere saying that `internal_url` is not meant for humans. It's the default URL used by the app when on the local network. Filling in `external_url` is only explained in the "remote access" section of the user manual.

I'm not entirely  sure what you mean now. Do you mean the Internal Connection URL which can be manually configured in the official mobile apps? If so, you can use any URL you want there, as long as it allows the mobile device to connect to Home Assistant, it doesn't have to be the same as the internal URL.

But again, the point of the `internal_url` and `external_url` is to make Home Assistant core able to tell other machines how they can reach Home Assistant. It's used to generate URLs, and it's included in mDNS announcements. Maybe this should be made more clear in the  documentation.

> I personally won't be changing my configuration regardless since it works fine as is

Sure, no one is forcing you to change a working configuration.

> You guys need to update a lot of documentation

Yes, agreed the documentation is confusing, help with updating it is always welcome.

I have opened a few PRs to adjust the documentation, help with review is welcome:
https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant.io/pull/38071
https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant.io/pull/38072
